Trust Engineering: Why your AI fails (and how to build systems that support production)

The video travels through Trust Engineering in four modules: silent crash, failure of intention that does not generate error; mapping of the real system before modernizing; deterministic architecture, with separation between brain and window and the threshold of 98% certainty; and orchestration of the intention with development oriented to specifications.

Published in 21 June 2026 · 10 min 27 s

  • Agentic engineering
  • Specification and development

Open on YouTube

The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets lead to the stretch of the video.

  1. From magic to engineering

  3. The AI as an amplifier
  4. Module 1: Map the truth
  5. Module 2: Architecture of trust

  8. Frequently Asked Questions

From magic to engineering

The video proposes treating AI not as magic, but as engineering discipline. Demonstrations seem sorcery; the challenge is to transform this charm into trust and predictability 00:00. The path goes from human intent to autonomous agentic execution 00:22.

The silent crash

When traditional software breaks down, the error makes noise: servers fall, screens freeze, alerts go off. With AI, failure almost never seems broken code; it is subtle and therefore dangerous 00:45.

Silent crash is a failure of intent, not code. Business value is lost without any errors on screen or log 01:05. The perfect demonstration can hide a system that perfectly executes the wrong business rule: the code compiles, the text comes out well formatted, but the decision breaks invisible rules without lighting alarm 01:25.

The journey has four stages: the risk of silent crash, mapping the truth, architecting confidence and orchestrating intention 01:46.

The AI as an amplifier

On the one hand, the AI as magic: systems made with loose prompts, which open the door to silent crashes, processing loops and cloud accounts that explode 02:07. On the other hand, AI as engineering: linear costs, reproducible flows and strict contracts that bar faults before they happen 02:27.

Capacity comes from the model; trust comes from engineering built around it 02:49.

The AI is an amplifier. With mapped processes and clarity, it scales clarity. With obscure rules and knowledge that only exists in the minds of a few people, it scales confusion, faster and with a face of competence 03:09. Clarity is not luxury: it is technical requirement 03:31.

Module 1: Map the truth

To build trust, the first step is to map the real state of the system, the current scenario, without any doubt. 03:31.

For this, a matrix of evidence is constructed that reveals tribal knowledge and hidden rules, crossing four sources. 03:52:

1. Structural inputs such as metadata and source code 03:52. 2. Status and configuration data in real time 04:15. 3. Operating logs, which show what really runs and what dead code is 04:154. 4. Tacit knowledge, extracted from historical and conversations with experts 04:15.

Together, these sources turn the fog into an inventory of auditable behavior 04:15.

Module 2: Architecture of trust

Real trust comes from system architecture, not just from models 04:37. It is born from a strict separation between the brain and the window 04:57.

The brain is the cognitive motor: heavy, asynchronous and sensitive, with access to critical data and business rules. The window is the public interface: light, agile and constantly changing 04:57.

The golden rule: the window never accesses the databases directly, and the brain never trusts with its eyes closed in what comes through the interface. This wall prevents a failure in exposure from breaking the core of the system 05:20.

The heart of risk control is the 98% threshold of certainty. If the confidence of an inference falls below 98% in a critical process, the machine loses its autonomy to decide 05:40.

Then comes the failed-closed governance, made to fail securely and predictably: uncertain exits are intercepted before they become facts in the system 06:01.

A strict scheme acts as a firewall. Everything that can be resolved with fixed data and rules is processed deterministically; the AI only remains the interpretative residue 06:22. If the response to this residue does not reach the target, the operation is degraded, paused or sent to a person 06:22.

An analogy: a Formula 1 car does not run at 300 km/h despite brakes, but because of them 06:43. Knowing that restrictions and validations fail safely is what enables us to accelerate innovation without fear of irreversible disaster 07:04.

Module 3: orchestrate intention

The professional evolves from executioner to cognitive orchestrator 07:04. In the analogy of the restaurant, the customer represents the business and focuses on value; the AI is the cook, who performs with technique and speed 07:25. The person assumes the role of chef: judges, understands the context, defines restrictions and aligns guidelines 07:47.

The mastery ceases to be typing code and becomes orchestrating the machine that generates the code 07:47.

In practice, this happens with specification-oriented development in four steps. 08:08:

1. Spec: intent is structured and becomes the source of truth 08:08. 2. Search: the relevant context of the system is recovered 08:28. 3. Execution: Agents edit files following what has been specified 08:28. 4. Validation: Automatic tests prove the result 08:28.

Maintained over time, this control creates an arsenal of organizational intelligence, with three components 08:50:

  • Skills: Machine reusable procedures such as mass testing 09:10.
  • Playbooks: Flow revenue, which guide audits and integrations 09:10.
  • Knowledge: standards, architectural decisions and accumulated documentation 09:10.

Instead of the guidelines getting lost in conversations with bots, the technical knowledge gets versioned and preserved 09:30.

Disposable prompt or versioned specification?

The final provocation: intention lives in a prompt that goes to waste in the next hour, or in a specification that the organization versions, audits and reuses 09:30? ? Recording the context rigorously and giving deterministic limits to the machine is not bureaucracy: it is what makes confidence climb together with the AI 09:51.

This engineering of trust is what separates prototypes from robust systems 10:13.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the silent crash?

A failure of intent: the system executes the wrong rule without any error on screen or log, and the business value is lost without alarm 01:05.

What happens when the AI is below 98% sure?

In a critical process, she loses her autonomy to decide: the operation is degraded, paused or sent for human review 05:40.

About the video

Your AI fails unannounced? The code compiles, the demo enchants, but the end result is logically wrong? Welcome to "Crash Silent" — the failure of intent that costs millions and nobody realizes until it's too late
.
In this video, we explore why Artificial Intelligence is an amplifier: if you deliver clarity, it scales clarity; if it delivers confusion, it scales confusion with a dangerous appearance of competence
. The solution is not "prompts smarter", but a disciplined architecture. As we say in the Intensive Systems Model (ISM) v1.0: "Capacity comes from the model; confidence comes from engineering"
.
What you will learn in this video:
Module 0 Understand the hidden cost of failure of intent and why the absence of error is not absence of failure
.
Module 1 How to use AI to reveal knowledge "tribal" hidden in legacy systems (As-Is) before trying to modernise them (To-Be)
.
Module 2 The principles of the First Deterministic, the physical separation between Brain and Vitrine and the use of strict contracts (schemes) to stop hallucinations before they reach the customer
.
Module 3 The transition from developer "executor" to Chef/Orchestrator, using Spec-Driven Development (SDD) to make specification the only source of truth
.
Content Highlights:
The F1: Why restrictions and governance are not to delay you, but to allow you to safely innovate at high speed
.
MCP protocol: The new security and interoperability border for AI agents
.
Vibe Coding: How to govern intention with the same discipline with which you ruled syntax
.
Video Chapters: 0:00 - The illusion of AI as "magic" 0:45 - The danger of Silent Crash
02:15 - AI as Amplifier of Clearness or Chaos
04:30 - M1: Revealing the Implicit (Reverse Engineering)
07:00 - M2: The Deterministic Pipeline and the 98% Sure Threshold
10:30 - M3: From Executor to Cognitive Orchestrator (SDD)
13:00 - The Future: Intentional Systems vs. Probabilistic Systems
